strategy: Add one closed starter-host-command@1 JSON transport above StarterHostOrchestrator and one root `skillctl.py host` stdio/file CLI. The transport validates exact fields and operation-specific payloads, dispatches only to existing Orchestrator methods, and returns a closed response containing the canonical session and next action. The CLI loads an explicitly operator-selected trusted factory outside the request envelope; it never performs semantic routing or constructs substitute execution authority.

changes.responsibility: validate the closed command envelope, map fixed operations to existing Orchestrator transitions, and project closed success/error responses
changes.reason: all Host wrappers need one shared transport contract instead of duplicating dispatch logic

changes.responsibility: provide a deterministic JSON stdin/file CLI and load one explicitly trusted Orchestrator factory
changes.reason: ChatGPT and Codex require a stable process boundary that can be invoked without importing internal controllers

changes.responsibility: publish closed request/response envelopes and fixed non-authority policy
changes.reason: Host integrations need a versioned reviewable wire contract

changes.responsibility: forward the canonical root `host` command to the new CLI
changes.reason: all supported Hosts must use the same root control plane

changes.responsibility: prove every operation mapping, exact payload closure, revision propagation, factory isolation, error redaction, and root CLI behavior
changes.reason: the new external boundary must fail closed under malformed or hostile commands

changes.responsibility: document natural-language and explicit-command interaction, bootstrap injection, wait/resume, extension, and standalone output boundaries
changes.reason: operators need concrete examples for ChatGPT, Codex, and project-specific adapters

changes.responsibility: link the completed CLI transport while retaining Orchestrator authority limits
changes.reason: the architecture record must match the executable integration layer

unchanged_boundaries: ChatGPT/Codex remains the semantic interpreter and selects only an exact verified Starter candidate
StarterHostOrchestrator remains session order and transition owner
StarterWorkflowRuntime and LangGraph remain Workflow execution authorities
DurableHostSkillBridge remains real Host Skill result and receipt transport
Provider adapters remain effect implementations selected through Capability activation
existing WriteAuthorityGuard remains the only mutating dispatch authorization boundary
TaskRun remains lifecycle and completion authority
external waits remain event-driven and Human Gates require explicit evidence
Graph END remains VALIDATING and no merge adapter or automatic merge is added
customer application source and runtime dependencies remain unchanged and independently runnable
forbidden_repairs: Do not add keyword, fuzzy, or model-independent natural-language routing.
Do not accept a factory/module/path from the untrusted JSON command envelope.
Do not expose arbitrary Python method names or generic reflection dispatch.
Do not auto-fill revisions, confirmations, evidence, correlation IDs, Host results, external events, or Human decisions.
Do not add a second Runtime, TaskRun writer, write guard, completion controller, release authority, or merge path.
Do not log secrets, factory objects, tracebacks, or arbitrary exception bodies in the wire response.
Do not modify customer Agent product code or generated standalone runtime dependencies.
required_invariants: the command envelope is closed and binds schema, command ID, Host, operation, session, expected revision, payload, and authority_effect false
each operation accepts exactly its documented payload fields and required revision semantics
transport dispatch calls only the matching public StarterHostOrchestrator method
the response carries the canonical session and re-derived next_action without reinterpretation
the trusted factory is selected only by an explicit CLI option or operator environment outside the request
CLI failures are deterministic, non-authorizing, nonzero, and do not leak secrets or tracebacks
transport retries rely on Orchestrator CAS/reconcile and never blindly replay or rewrite revisions
selection and confirmation still grant no write authority and no automatic merge exists

focused: OPEN and READ commands preserve natural language and return the canonical selection/session
SELECT, CONFIRM, START, Host result, external event, Human decision, and RECONCILE map exact revisions and payloads to the corresponding Orchestrator methods
root skillctl host reads one JSON command and emits one closed JSON response through an injected trusted factory
counterexamples: unknown fields, operation, Host, schema, policy, missing or forbidden revision, and malformed operation payload are rejected before dispatch
factory identifiers inside the request, arbitrary method names, implicit selection, missing evidence, and wrong correlation shapes are rejected
factory load errors and Orchestrator errors produce bounded non-secret failures and nonzero exit status
regression: Host Orchestrator, Starter runtime, selection, Host bridge, Provider bootstrap, TaskRun, and root CLI suites remain green
complete Skill unit and all required skill-only profiles remain green
negative_path: transport never interprets user language or executes arbitrary commands
transport cannot grant write authority, complete a TaskRun, or merge a PR
external waits and Human Gates cannot advance without exact durable evidence
standalone customer application source and dependencies remain unchanged

risks: A trusted factory may be project-specific; selecting it is an operator/bootstrap responsibility and not part of untrusted request data.
One-shot CLI calls may lose stdout after a committed transition; the caller must READ and, only for claimed transitions, RECONCILE using the durable session revision.
The wire contract proves repository-visible validation and dispatch, not private model reasoning.
rollback_plan: Remove the Host transport/CLI modules, schema, tests, root command mapping, and transport architecture record. StarterHostOrchestrator and all lower execution boundaries continue to operate through their existing Python APIs.
